learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Exploration progress is not mastery evidence; quiz attempts remain the scored retrieval signal.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: VPC CIDR → subnet CIDRs → ENI private __________.

reveal.text: Subnets carve the VPC address space into Availability-Zone-scoped networks for resources.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Public subnet = route to an internet gateway plus resource/public-address requirements; subnet itself is not “public” by __________.

reveal.text: Internet reachability depends on routing and the resource’s addressing/security configuration.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Deployment fails with insufficient addresses → check subnet free __________.

reveal.text: CIDR sizing and available IP addresses matter operationally.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Destination CIDR/prefix → next-hop __________.

reveal.text: Route tables determine where subnet/ENI traffic is directed.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Most specific matching route __________.

reveal.text: Routing chooses the most specific matching route.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Packets never reach NAT/IGW/TGW” → inspect __________.

reveal.text: Route tables are one of the first checks.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Stateful virtual firewall at ENI/resource __________.

reveal.text: Security groups control allowed inbound/outbound traffic and are stateful.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Return traffic for an allowed flow is automatically __________.

reveal.text: Stateful behavior tracks permitted connections.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Security group rules are allow-only; no explicit __________ rules.

reveal.text: Network ACLs support allow and deny entries.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Stateless subnet-level allow/deny __________.

reveal.text: Network ACLs filter traffic entering/leaving subnets using numbered rules.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Because NACLs are stateless, allow both request and return __________.

reveal.text: Return-path ephemeral ports/directions must be permitted as required.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Security group / NACL

nodes.title: Internet gateway, NAT, and egress-only IGW

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: IGW / NAT Gateway / Egress-only IGW

columns.title: Internet Gateway
items: public IPv4/IPv6 internet path for addressed resources

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Private IPv4 instances need outbound internet updates, no inbound internet → __________.

reveal.text: Use a NAT gateway in an appropriate public subnet plus routes.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Private IPv6 egress-only internet → __________.

reveal.text: Use an egress-only internet gateway.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Gateway endpoint / interface endpoint

columns.title: Gateway endpoint
items: route-table target for supported services such as S3/DynamoDB

columns.title: Interface endpoint
items: ENIs powered by PrivateLink for supported services

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Access supported AWS service privately without NAT/internet → __________.

reveal.text: A VPC endpoint is a key clue.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: PrivateLink provides service connectivity; it is not full VPC-to-VPC __________.

reveal.text: Use peering/TGW/VPN/DX for broader network connectivity patterns.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Private IP connectivity between two VPCs via a non-transitive __________.

reveal.text: VPC peering directly connects two VPCs; routing and security must allow traffic.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Peering is non-__________.

reveal.text: You cannot use one peered VPC as a transit router for another peer.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Small number of direct VPC pairs → peering may be simpler than __________.

reveal.text: Transit Gateway becomes attractive as connectivity grows into a hub-and-spoke topology.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Hub for connecting many VPCs and on-premises __________.

reveal.text: Transit Gateway provides centralized routing among attached networks.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Many VPCs with complex mesh peering → consider __________.

reveal.text: Transit Gateway can reduce pairwise connectivity complexity.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Attachment + TGW route table + propagation/association → __________.

reveal.text: Troubleshoot both attachment state and Transit Gateway routing.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: WAF / Shield / Network Firewall / DNS Firewall

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: SQL injection/web path rules → __________.

reveal.text: AWS WAF.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Filter DNS queries to malicious domains → __________.

reveal.text: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: NAT processing, cross-AZ/Region transfer, public egress, and duplicated __________.

reveal.text: Network cost depends heavily on traffic path, transfer direction, and intermediaries.

prompts.label: ⚡ ACTION
prompts.placeholder: Keep high-volume traffic on efficient/private paths where that reduces data-processing/transfer __________.

reveal.text: Evaluate endpoints, topology, AZ placement, CloudFront, and architecture against actual traffic.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Cheapest path is not automatically the most resilient/secure __________.

reveal.text: Optimize cost within availability, security, and performance requirements.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Domain → hosted zone → DNS record → __________.

reveal.text: DNS records map names to values/targets according to record type and routing policy.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Public hosted zone / private hosted zone

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Alias record can point to supported AWS resources without exposing a fixed __________.

reveal.text: Alias records integrate directly with supported AWS targets.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Inbound endpoint: on-prem → VPC DNS; outbound endpoint: VPC → on-prem DNS.

columns.title: Outbound
items: VPC queries forwarded to external/on-prem DNS

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Hybrid DNS between VPC and on-prem domains → __________.

reveal.text: Use Route 53 Resolver endpoints/rules.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Resolver endpoint is not a general-purpose TCP/IP __________.

reveal.text: It is for DNS query resolution/forwarding.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Weighted / latency / failover / geolocation / geoproximity / multivalue

reveal.text: Weighted routing.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Send users to Region with lowest latency” → __________.

reveal.text: Latency-based routing.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Capture DNS queries for visibility/troubleshooting and security __________.

reveal.text: Route 53 Resolver query logging records DNS queries from configured VPC resources.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Need to know which domains workloads are resolving → __________.

reveal.text: Enable Resolver query logging for the relevant VPCs.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Query logging is not the same as VPC Flow Logs, which record network flow __________.

reveal.text: Use the log source that matches the question.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: CDN that caches/serves content through global edge __________.

reveal.text: CloudFront accelerates HTTP(S) content delivery and can protect/origin-shield applications with integrated features.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Viewer → edge → origin

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: CloudFront / Global Accelerator

columns.title: Global Accelerator
items: network acceleration to application endpoints using static anycast IPs

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Cache key includes selected headers/cookies/query strings; extra variance lowers cache __________.

reveal.text: Keep the cache key only as variable as the application requires.

prompts.label: ⚡ ACTION
prompts.placeholder: Stale cached object after urgent update → use invalidation or versioned object __________.

reveal.text: Control freshness with TTLs, invalidations, and versioned filenames/keys as appropriate.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Origin request policy can forward values without making them part of the cache __________.

reveal.text: Separate cache variation from origin forwarding needs.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Static anycast IP entry points route traffic across the AWS global __________.

reveal.text: Global Accelerator improves availability/performance for supported application endpoints using AWS global network routing.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Need static global IPs and accelerate TCP/UDP or non-cacheable app traffic → __________.

reveal.text: Global Accelerator is a strong clue.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Global Accelerator does not cache web objects like __________.

reveal.text: CloudFront provides CDN caching.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Source → route → security controls → middleboxes/gateways → destination → return __________.

reveal.text: Validate every hop and the return path; networking failures are often asymmetric.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Check DNS, routes, SGs, NACLs, target/service health, and __________.

reveal.text: Also inspect NAT/TGW/endpoints/firewalls and return routing where present.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Opening every port is not a valid troubleshooting __________.

reveal.text: Diagnose the actual blocking control and preserve least privilege.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Network flow metadata such as source/destination, ports, protocol, and accept/reject __________.

reveal.text: VPC Flow Logs capture metadata for IP traffic at supported VPC networking scopes.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use to verify whether traffic is reaching an ENI/subnet/VPC and whether it is accepted/rejected.

reveal.text: Flow records help narrow down network path and security-control issues.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Flow Logs do not capture full packet payload __________.

reveal.text: They are flow metadata, not packet capture.

nodes.title: ELB, WAF, CloudFront, and container logs

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Pick logs at the layer where the failure is __________.

reveal.text: ELB access logs show load-balancer requests; WAF logs show web ACL decisions; CloudFront logs show edge requests; app/container logs show workload behavior.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Client reached edge but origin returned error → correlate CloudFront/ELB/app __________.

reveal.text: Cross-layer correlation helps identify where the request failed.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: One log source rarely explains an entire multi-tier request __________.

reveal.text: Correlate request IDs/timestamps where possible.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Static configuration analysis of network __________ between source and destination.

reveal.text: Reachability Analyzer analyzes the configured path and identifies blocking/missing components without sending packets.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: “Which route/SG/NACL component prevents connectivity?” → __________.

reveal.text: VPC Reachability Analyzer is a strong diagnostic tool.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: It is not an end-to-end live latency/performance __________.

reveal.text: Use monitoring/synthetic/flow tools for live behavior.

nodes.title: Hybrid connectivity: Direct Connect and VPN

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Direct Connect / Site-to-Site VPN

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Hybrid troubleshooting includes BGP/routes, tunnel/virtual interface state, on-prem firewall, and __________.

reveal.text: Validate both AWS and on-premises routing/security plus redundancy.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Dedicated private circuit” → __________; “encrypted tunnels over internet” → __________.

reveal.text: Direct Connect; Site-to-Site VPN.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Endpoint policy, DNS, route table, SGs, service support, peering/TGW routes, and __________.

reveal.text: Private connectivity requires both correct path configuration and authorization/service-specific settings.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Interface endpoint resolves publicly instead of privately → check private DNS and __________.

reveal.text: Check endpoint configuration, VPC DNS settings, and the name being resolved.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: A VPC endpoint does not make every AWS service privately reachable by __________.

reveal.text: Only supported endpoint services and configured endpoints are available through that path.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Unexpected stale/wrong variants: TTL, cache key, origin headers/cookies/query strings, invalidation, and __________.

reveal.text: Verify behavior/path pattern and which policy controls caching/forwarding.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Origin has new file but users still see old content” → inspect cache freshness/invalidation.

reveal.text: CloudFront cache behavior is the focus.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Changing origin content does not necessarily purge existing edge __________.

reveal.text: Cached objects remain until expiration/invalidation/versioned URL changes.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Helps monitor network flows and identify performance/network-health __________.

reveal.text: Network Flow Monitor provides network flow performance visibility for supported AWS workloads.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use when you need flow-level network performance visibility rather than only accept/reject __________.

reveal.text: It complements VPC Flow Logs with performance-oriented monitoring.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Network Flow Monitor ≠ VPC Flow Logs.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Observes how internet performance/availability affects application traffic from user __________.

reveal.text: Internet Monitor provides visibility into internet paths and end-user network performance for monitored applications.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Users in a geography report internet-path degradation but AWS resource metrics look healthy → __________.

reveal.text: Internet Monitor is a strong clue.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: It is not DNS routing configuration itself.

reveal.text: Use it for visibility/analysis; use Route 53/CloudFront/Global Accelerator or architecture changes for remediation as appropriate.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Runs synthetic network tests between configured endpoints to measure reachability/performance __________.

reveal.text: Network Synthetic Monitor actively probes configured hybrid network paths, such as from AWS resources toward on-premises destination IP addresses, to measure latency and packet loss.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Need proactive scheduled path tests rather than waiting for user traffic → __________.

reveal.text: Use it when you need proactive, repeatable monitoring of hybrid network connectivity instead of waiting for real user traffic.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Synthetic tests are active probes; Flow Logs are passive traffic __________.

reveal.text: Choose based on whether you need generated tests or observations of real traffic.
